intro: A cup of mango smoothie from a shop is about 300 kcal (estimate). Most of it comes from the mango, sugar syrup and the milk or yogurt blended in.
diet: Yes, but count it like a big snack or half a meal. It sounds healthy because there's fruit, but there's often a lot of added sugar. If you have one, treat it as your afternoon snack, not a drink on the side with lunch.
tips: Pick the smallest size and ask for less syrup.
Skip ice cream or whipped cream toppings.
Make your own: frozen mango + plain yogurt + a little milk, no sugar.

swap.name: Cut mango + plain yogurt
swap.why: You still get the mango taste, more protein from the yogurt, and no sugar syrup.

faq.a: Once in a while, yes, but most shop smoothies are low in protein. Better to have it with eggs or bread with some protein.

faq.q: Which mango is best for smoothies?
faq.a: Harum manis or any mango that's properly ripe. Frozen mango works well too, since you don't need much ice.

faq.q: What's the difference between a smoothie and juice?
faq.a: A smoothie blends the whole fruit, so the fibre stays. Juice is usually strained and has less fibre.
